What you’ll actually do
As a Senior Product Engineer at Modash, you’ll work closely with product and engineers to turn messy customer problems into simple, useful product experiences.
Depending on the team, you might work on:

•
Discovery: creator search that makes the product value obvious in the first session.

•
CRM: relationship management and outreach tools that make teams forget about existence of Google Sheets.

•
Campaigns: performance aggregation across millions of pieces of creator content, helping customers see what worked and what to do next.

•
Creator: affiliate management, attribution, and payouts that make Modash the easiest way for brands to pay creators.

The problems we work on will change. The need for strong sense of ownership will not.
You will be expected to:

•
Turn customer pain into product decisions. Understand what users are trying to do, where they get stuck, and what the simplest useful solution looks like.

•
Own work from problem to production. Shape the approach, build the solution, ship it, measure what happens, and improve it based on feedback.

•
Work across the stack and make tradeoffs clearly. Move between frontend, backend, infrastructure, data modeling, debugging, and handling product decisions depending on what the problem needs.

•
Raise the quality of decisions around you. Ask better questions, challenge weak assumptions, give useful feedback, and help the team keep momentum without waiting for perfect certainty.

Requirements
You’ll do well here if...
The best Senior Product Engineers here don’t wait for perfect context. They get close to the customer, make sharp tradeoffs, ship reliable systems, and stay accountable after launch.

• You have built and operated production systems that real users depend on.

• You have enough backend depth to design, build, and debug production services, APIs, data models, async work, and integrations. In practice, that usually means at least a couple of years of hands-on backend work.

• You care about product outcomes, not just technical elegance.

• You can learn whatever the problem requires, from frontend patterns to infrastructure, product domains, or AI-assisted workflows.

• You are comfortable with ambiguity and can create clarity for yourself and others.

• You work well with product designers and care about the quality of the customer experience.

You probably won’t enjoy this role if...

• You want a narrow frontend-only or backend-only lane. Here you own the stack end-to-end.

• You prefer detailed specs handed to you before you start working.

• You want the manager to decide your every next step.

• You want product managers and designers to define all the solutions before you get involved.

• You care more about technical elegance than customer outcomes.

Bonus points if...

• You have worked with Vue, Node.js, TypeScript, AWS, MongoDB, or ClickHouse.

WHO WE ARE

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, Booking.com http://Booking.com, H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

As Senior Data Journalist, you will build Imprint's data storytelling function from the ground up. This is a highly autonomous individual contributor role sitting at the intersection of data science and narrative journalism, the first of its kind at Imprint, and it calls for someone who can operate as a peer to the data science team, not just a consumer of what they hand off.

Working closely with data science, you will independently mine Imprint's payments, merchant, and card member data to surface stories that are credible, data-driven, and genuinely interesting, not promotional. This requires someone who can write production-grade SQL and dbt models themselves, design the analysis with statistical rigor, defend the methodology under scrutiny, and still land the story in clear, compelling prose. You'll set direction independently, hold a narrative strategy under competing priorities, and ship work consistently.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

- Built and operationalized a data room in partnership with the data science team, including the underlying SQL and dbt models needed to continuously mine and surface story candidates from Imprint's payments, merchant, and card member data

- Defined the core narrative pillars that will guide Imprint's data storytelling, grounded in the company's brand positioning and differentiated data position, with each pillar mapped to specific, defensible data sources and methodologies

- Developed an initial content calendar with proposed story formats and publishing cadence, and shipped at least one full story end to end, from raw data to published piece, demonstrating the full workflow

Responsibilities

- Write and produce data-driven stories that contribute meaningfully to public discourse around how people live and buy today

- Own Imprint's data storytelling function end-to-end, from writing your own SQL and dbt models to story identification, statistical analysis, and publication

- Independently design and execute the analytical approach for each story, including sampling methodology, statistical significance, and handling of outliers or data quality issues

- Partner with the data science team as a technical peer to build and maintain infrastructure for ongoing story mining across Imprint's proprietary data sets

- Propose and iterate on story formats, publishing cadence, and distribution approach

- Maintain editorial independence: push back on ad hoc data requests that fall outside the narrative strategy

- Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders, including communications, brand, product marketing, data science, and leadership, to share findings and determine the best ways to distribute stories

Centralized monitoring is an integral part of risk-based monitoring strategy, defined as the timely, remote review of accumulating subject and operational data to help distinguish between reliable and unreliable data, trends, outliers and unusual variability using analytics and statistical methods.
